gap_analysis.objective: Run one sealed-bid second-price round with three live LLM bidders and compare their bids, winner, payment, and payoffs against a post-commitment truthful-bidding reference.

requirement.description: Three LLM bidders each submit one scalar sealed bid from private valuations through live schema-constrained decisions.
required_guarantees: private valuations never shared across actors before commitment

decisions.reason: llm.v1 gives schema-constrained per-actor LLM decisions with bounded retries through the credential-isolated host relay, with reasoning_effort null and max_output_tokens 2000.

requirement.description: One simultaneous round collecting exactly one action per bidder with no sequential leakage.

decisions.reason: simultaneous.v1 with rounds=1 collects one joint batch; the simultaneous schedule plus per-actor observation permissions implements sealed bidding.

requirement.description: Finite-nonnegative bid domain with highest-wins, second-price payment, quasi-linear utilities, and configuration-order tie-breaks, reusable across bidders and valuations.
required_guarantees: reusable across configured bidders and valuations

decisions.reason: No inventory mechanism implements second-price auctions; extend Mechanism with a reusable settlement plus its bid action schema and parameter schema.

requirement.description: Post-commitment truthful-bidding reference (bids equal valuations, winner, payment, utilities) with a weak-dominance explanation.

decisions.reason: A small pure utility computed after commitment suffices; no Nash solver or GameView is needed and benchmark stays null.

requirement.description: Custom verification of allocation, payment, utilities, tie-breaks, bid legality, and observation privacy.

decisions.reason: Piecewise auction rules do not fit the numeric-expression problem language, so a VerificationCheck subclass recomputes the settlement independently from committed actions and recorded observations.

requirement.description: Executed notebook comparing actual bids, winner, payment, payoffs, and rationales against the truthful reference.
constraints: no actor or model calls from notebook cells

decisions.reason: Compose reporting result helpers with the auction truthful-reference utility and matplotlib comparisons in a generator that reads only the recorded result.

components.purpose: Finite nonnegative sealed-bid payload; bids above or below valuation stay legal.

acceptance_tests.name: test_bid_schema_accepts_finite_nonnegative
acceptance_tests.expected: Finite nonnegative bids validate, including zero and integer-valued bids.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: a bid is a finite nonnegative number.

acceptance_tests.name: test_bid_schema_rejects_invalid_bids
acceptance_tests.expected: Negative, NaN, infinite, boolean, string, and missing bids raise validation errors.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: a bid is a finite nonnegative number.

acceptance_tests.name: test_bid_schema_preserves_exact_amount
acceptance_tests.expected: Validation keeps the exact submitted amount without rounding, clamping, or defaulting.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: the winner pays the second-highest submitted bid exactly.

components.purpose: Reusable second-price settlement: highest bid wins, pays the second-highest bid, configuration-order tie-breaks, and quasi-linear utilities from private valuations.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_settles_second_price
acceptance_tests.expected: Highest bid wins and pays the second-highest bid; the winner earns valuation minus payment and losers earn zero.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: highest bid wins, pays the second-highest bid; utility is own valuation minus payment, others zero.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_breaks_ties_by_config_order
acceptance_tests.expected: Tied highest bids resolve to the earliest bidder in configuration order with payment equal to the tied amount.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: break highest-bid ties by configuration order.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_allows_strategically_poor_bids
acceptance_tests.expected: Bids above valuation (even with negative winner utility) and below valuation validate and settle normally.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: do not reject a bid merely because it is strategically poor.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_illegal_actions
acceptance_tests.expected: Negative or nonfinite bids, wrong action kinds, incomplete profiles, and unknown actors raise errors.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rules: finite nonnegative bids with one action per bidder in a single sealed round.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_reusable_across_valuations
acceptance_tests.expected: Changed valuations, bids, and tie-break orders settle from configuration with no hardcoded winner or payment.
acceptance_tests.reference: User requirement: keep auction rules reusable across configured bidders and valuations.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_records_history_and_state
acceptance_tests.expected: Transition appends the bid profile and records winner, payment, and payoffs; state validation accepts the result and rejects tampered records.
acceptance_tests.reference: User requirements: recording runtime interfaces with custom verification of allocation, payment, and utilities.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_config_enforces_sealed_observations
acceptance_tests.expected: The draft configuration validates and each bidder observes only the public rules plus its own valuation and memory.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: bidders see the auction rules and only their own private valuation and memory.

components.purpose: Reusable auction configuration: record field names, tie-break order, and the pricing, values, utility, item, reserve, and budget conventions.

acceptance_tests.name: test_auction_params_accepts_reusable_config
acceptance_tests.expected: A full auction configuration validates, and omitted field names fall back to documented defaults.
acceptance_tests.reference: User requirement: record textbook conventions and the tie-break convention in configuration.

acceptance_tests.name: test_auction_params_rejects_bad_config
acceptance_tests.expected: Duplicate or empty tie-break entries, unknown pricing or values models, nonzero reserve, and clashing field names raise errors.
acceptance_tests.reference: User requirements: no reserve, second-price payment, configuration-order tie-breaks.

components.purpose: Pure post-commitment truthful-bidding reference mapping valuations and bidder order to bids, winner, payment, and utilities.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_matches_valuations
acceptance_tests.expected: Truthful bids equal valuations with winner, payment, and utilities matching second-price arithmetic on 90, 65, and 40.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: compute the truthful-bidding reference from private valuations after commitment.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_breaks_ties_by_order
acceptance_tests.expected: Equal valuations resolve by the supplied bidder order with payment equal to the tied value.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: break highest-bid ties by configuration order.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_rejects_invalid_inputs
acceptance_tests.expected: Empty, mismatched, negative, or nonfinite valuations or orders raise errors.
acceptance_tests.reference: User rule: truthful bids are finite nonnegative valuations over exactly the configured bidders.

custom_checks.purpose: Independently recompute winner, payment, and utilities from committed bids and initial private valuations with configuration-order tie-breaks; verify bid legality and that recorded observations exposed only each bidder's own valuation.
